subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - FinTechX
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Thompson <alyssa@fintechx.com>, John Rivera <john@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - recap & next steps

Hi Alyssa / John - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the immediate asks so we can put together a tailored Dedicated capacity proposal.

Call recap
- Primary use case: real-time pricing & fraud scoring for transaction flows (low variance prompts, avg context ~128 tokens).
- Current monthly usage: ~60M tokens today; growth expectations: ~300M tokens/month within 6-12 months (usage spikes around batch runs / month-end).
- Peak traffic profile: expected peak ~70-90 requests/sec; avg request size ~128 tokens; latency target for real-time paths: p95 < 250ms.
- Security: VPC private deployment is likely (we discussed Private vs Dedicated) - for now focus on Dedicated reserved capacity for predictability.

Open items you asked us to confirm
1) Budget range you have for inference: you mentioned $25k- $40k/month as a starting point for the project budget.
2) Target unit economics / target $ per 1M tokens: you called out a goal of ~$30/1M tokens.
3) Preference / constraints for GPU vendor (A100 vs H100) and reservation size: you wanted options and unit-cost estimates.

What we need from you to finalize a proposal
- Confirmation of target monthly tokens to price to (we used 300M as our working figure).
- Any hard latency SLOs beyond p95 < 250ms (e.g., p50 or p99 targets).
- Preference on GPU family (A100 vs H100) or willingness to evaluate both in the technical deep-dive.

Next steps
- I will share an initial pricing package + unit economics based on 300M tokens/month and two reference Dedicated configs (attached). [Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf]
- Marcus (cc) will run a short throughput/latency sizing run with your sample traces if you can share one (we flagged fintechx_usage_report_Q1.csv). [Attachment: fintechx_usage_report_Q1.csv]
- If the numbers look good, we'll circulate a draft SOW for term/commitment (attached draft). [Attachment: SOW-draft.docx]

Proposed timeline
- You confirm the target tokens and GPU preference by EOW (Fri 3/12)
- Marcus schedules a technical deep-dive next week to validate sizing
- We deliver a final pricing + SOW within 3 business days after the deep-dive

Thanks - I left the recommended pricing options and unit economics in the attached PDF but pasted a short summary in my follow-up.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf]

From: Alyssa Thompson <alyssa@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: John Rivera <john@fintechx.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa - that lines up with our notes. A couple clarifying points so you can tune the proposal: 

- Confirmed target tokens: we currently plan to budget for ~300M tokens/month as the baseline (we may size a bit higher for headroom).
- Budget: our procurement lead gave a soft range of $25k- $40k/month for inference costs (excluding SRE/infra labor).
- Unit economics: yes, our business is targeting ~ $30 / 1M tokens or better for operating economics; if you can get below that with Dedicated that would be compelling.
- Latency: p95 < 250ms is a hard SLO for the real-time scoring path. For async/batch paths latency less important.

One more ask: please give throughput expectations (tokens/sec and concurrent requests) for each GPU option, and an estimate for reserved capacity size (number of GPUs) that will meet our SLOs at 300M tokens/month. Also include any assumptions (avg seq len, batching, KV cache benefits).

Happy to do the deep-dive - Marcus, can you share an available slot next week?

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Thompson
Head of ML Engineering, FinTechX
alyssa@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Thompson <alyssa@fintechx.com>, John Rivera <john@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - proposed configs & unit economics

Alyssa - thanks for the clarity. Below are two practical Dedicated configurations and the unit-economics we expect based on your 300M tokens/month target. Assumptions: avg request size 128 tokens, peak concurrency ~80 rps, production batching that averages a 1.8x effective batching improvement, KV prefix cache for repeated prefixes (we conservatively modeled 10% cache hit).

Option A - A100 (reference)
- Hardware: 4 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (reserved cluster)
- Throughput: supports sustained ~45k tokens/sec aggregate with batching (peak short bursts up to ~65k tokens/sec)
- Latency: p95 estimated ~200-240ms for 128-token inference with continuous batching + optimized kernels
- Monthly capacity: comfortably handles 300M tokens/month with headroom (~20% buffer)
- Pricing (est): $27 / 1M tokens -> ~ $8,100 / month equivalent for model runtime; total monthly with reserved capacity, infra overhead and support: ~$29k/month

Option B - H100 (higher throughput)
- Hardware: 2 x NVIDIA H100 (note: H100 per-GPU throughput higher; fewer GPUs required for the same throughput depending on model)
- Throughput: supports sustained ~60k tokens/sec aggregate, bursts to ~90k tokens/sec
- Latency: p95 estimated ~150-200ms for 128-token inference
- Monthly capacity: covers 300M tokens/month with more headroom and lower unit compute cost
- Pricing (est): $20 / 1M tokens -> ~ $6,000 / month equivalent for model runtime; total monthly with reserved capacity, infra overhead and support: ~$24k/month

Notes & trade-offs
- A100 option is a more conservative, widely-available config and slightly simpler from a procurement standpoint.
- H100 yields better unit economics and lower p95 latency but procurement availability and pricing may vary by region and term.
- All prices above assume a 12-month reserved commit; shorter terms increase unit price ~15-25%.

Recommended next steps
1) Marcus to schedule a 60-min sizing run with your infra traces (Marcus, can you propose 2 slots next week?).
2) If FinTechX prefers H100, we'll model a 2-3 GPU config in the SOW and share final SOW + DocuSign link.
3) If you want further cost reduction targets (target <$18/1M), we can explore larger reserved pools + quantization or off-peak capacity routing.

I've attached the detailed pricing sheet and the usage report you shared - Marcus will kick off the sizing.

- Marissa
[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf]
[Attachment: fintechx_usage_report_Q1.csv]

From: John Rivera <john@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alyssa Thompson <alyssa@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - next steps

Marissa / Alyssa - thanks for the clear options. A few quick items from procurement and product: 

- Budget: the $24k- $29k/month bands are within the ballpark of what procurement expected; our preference is to maximize headroom while keeping to the lower end of budget if possible.
- GPU preference: we prefer H100 if Redwood can guarantee the unit economics you quoted in writing in the SOW (we need the $20/1M tokens figure to be explicit).
- SOW & timeline: please send the SOW and a DocuSign link. We'd like to start staging in April with a 30-day validation period.

Marcus - can you take point on the technical deep-dive Monday or Tuesday next week? Please include a quick checklist of the traces/configs you need.

Marissa - once we get the SOW I'll route internally and get procurement to review.

Thanks,
John Rivera
VP Product, FinTechX
john@fintechx.com
